co_monastery_the.blurb: The Monastery is a cluster of crags in Big Thompson Canyon, in the Estes Park Valley of Colorado, at roughly 7,800 feet. Reaching it takes a hike in of about 45 to 60 minutes. The climbing is almost all sport, with a small amount of trad, and the walls run from steep and edgy to slabby with good friction. Grades span 5.6 to 5.13, with the weight in the 5.7 to 5.11 range and a modest number of harder lines above. The crags are laid out in three rows split by two corridors, and The Vestibule and Lion's Den hold the most climbs, followed by Outer Gates and The Catacomb.

ct_sleeping_giant_state_park.blurb: Sleeping Giant State Park sits in Hamden, just north of New Haven, and has a long history as a climbing destination in Connecticut. Today it mixes boulder problems with trad lines and a few top-rope routes, and its small outcrops are decent for bouldering. Bouldering makes up the larger share, mostly in the lower V grades with a few hard problems, while the roped routes range from easy fifth class up to the low 5.11s. Between the Chin and Chest holds the most climbs, followed by Right Knee and The Chin.

ga_currahee_mountain.blurb: Currahee Mountain rises beside the town of Toccoa in northeast Georgia. The rock is mostly slab, so friction is the main skill, and boulders are scattered across the mountain. Climbing here is a blend of trad, sport and bouldering, with a few top-rope lines. Most roped routes are bolted to some degree, many have anchors that can be reached for top roping, and the roped climbs cluster around 5.10 and 5.11. Boulder problems run from V0 to V5. Brick Wall holds the most climbs and is shaded, while Middle Junction, the Main and Slab Wall area and The Buzzard Wall add more.

md_the_gunpowder_falls_bouldering_area.blurb: Bouldering in Gunpowder Falls State Park is spread along the Gunpowder River in northern Baltimore County rather than packed into one field. All of the problems are boulders, with a good spread from V0 to V6 and a handful much harder. At Hereford the boulders are schist of varying quality, with problems on both sides of the river, while Hazel's Rocks, on a hillside north of the river, is a mix of schist, metagreywacke and quartzite. Around The Fin there are scattered boulders beside a few rope climbs. Hereford Hill and Angler's Bluffs hold the most problems, followed by Fin Bouldering and Hazel's Rocks.

_expect.name: Cavalry Boulder Field aka Gymnasium aka Playground

ma_cavalry_boulder_field_aka_gymnasium_a.blurb: Cavalry Boulder Field lies in the Tompson Street Reservation in Gloucester, on Cape Ann, and is shaded by hemlocks. The terrain is varied and the difficulty range is wide, with nearly everything a boulder problem. Grades run from V0 to V10, with the bulk between V3 and V5 and a smaller number of harder problems. The reservation is rugged, with exposed granite outcroppings throughout, and granite is the rock of Cape Ann's boulders and short cliffs. The Central Sector holds the most problems, followed by the North Sector, while the East, South and West sectors have only a few.
